input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser only splits input on "\n" and never strips "\r". The new Windows-based accounting export tool almost certainly writes CRLF line endings, so each line (including the header line) ends with a trailing "\r". That makes the last header column become "description\r" instead of "description", so `REQUIRED_COLUMNS.some(column => !header.includes(column))` in `assertShape` evaluates to true and `IngestError("errors.rowShape", { row: 1 })` is thrown immediately — exactly matching the reported "Malformed row" on row 1 for every file.

Fix: normalize line endings (e.g. strip "\r" when splitting, or split on /\r?\n/) before parsing the header and rows in `src/ingest/parser.ts`.
